QF.id: Duplicate Share Certificates and Transmission of Securities_7

question.text: What is the key difference between transfer and transmission of securities?

answer.text: Transfer is automatic while transmission requires approval
Transfer applies only to demat shares while transmission applies only to physical shares
Transfer requires court orders while transmission does not
Transfer is a voluntary act between parties while transmission occurs by operation of law such as on death of a holder

explanation.text: The Logic: Transfer is the change of ownership of securities through stock-market or off-market transactions and is carried out using an instrument of transfer. Transmission, by contrast, deals with the devolution of securities through inheritance, succession or on the death of a holder. The Trap: Treating transfer and transmission as interchangeable terms misses the point. Transfer is a deliberate transaction between parties; transmission occurs by operation of law when the holder dies or in similar succession situations. Note: The transfer procedure using an instrument of transfer is covered on pages 149-150, and the death/inheritance transmission process is covered on pages 156-157 of the NISM-Series-II-A Registrars and Transfer Agents (Corporate) Certification Examination workbook (October 2025).
